Two search methods, a sampler, and an error method solve it in rough form. Tests on fake brain signals show sharper place and contrast in rebuilt images.
arxiv-2603-19480: Sudijono and co-authors study regression adjustments for double randomization in two-sided marketplaces. Such designs handle interference, where one user's treatment affects others. The team derives estimators with the smallest asymptotic variance among linear adjusted ones. No linear model on outcomes is assumed. The best adjustments differ from those in classic trials and can be estimated from data. One direct-effect estimator uses a weighted regression with two-way fixed effects. Simulations show large efficiency gains over simpler methods.
arxiv-2603-19680: Mondal and Hou study higher-order flow in dilepton emission from a magnetized hot hadronic medium. Dileptons probe the matter made in heavy-ion collisions. A background magnetic field can imprint direction patterns on the emission. The team computes source-level flow coefficients beyond elliptic flow, up to sixth order. Odd-order coefficients vanish by symmetry, they find. The even ones show rich structure at low invariant mass, driven by Landau levels of pions. At higher masses the effects fade, making dileptons a sensitive probe of field strength.
arxiv-2603-20180: Huang and co-authors pick frames for long video question answering with a greedy method that balances relevance and coverage. Vision language models slow down as frame counts and visual tokens grow. Sparse sampling can miss the decisive moment in a video. Pure relevance ranking tends to pick near duplicate frames instead. Their method scores candidate frames in two embedding spaces, one for question fit and one for semantic spread. A submodular objective yields a greedy pick with a known approximation guarantee.
arxiv-2603-20380: Agostino and D'Souza apply a radiation safety idea to managing multi-agent AI teams. The ALARA rule keeps exposure as low as reasonably achievable. Their version keeps agent context lean through a plain-text data layer. Users declare each agent's tool access directly and can edit the tools. A shell program, npcsh, loads the team and runs the agents. Tests covered 22 local models on 115 practical tasks. The tasks spanned file work, web search, scripting, and delegation.
arxiv-2603-20880: Silva and co-authors extend the Euler-Heisenberg action to backgrounds that break Lorentz symmetry. These backgrounds vary across spacetime and act as fixed anisotropies. They compute the correction with a spectral method applied to the modified Dirac operator, inside the Standard Model Extension framework. Results go to second order in the background terms. They find Furry's theorem can fail at second order for some term mixes, and axion like terms appear in the action. They also derive the changed Maxwell equations and a local dispersion relation.
arxiv-2603-20980: Zaytsev and co-authors present DCNAR, a two stage method that learns causal structure in neural time series and then does causal inference with it. Most dynamic causal models assume the network is known in advance, which is rarely true. First, a neural model learns a sparse directed causal network from multivariate series. That structure then guides a time varying network autoregression. On multi-country panel data, the learned networks give more stable and meaningful causal estimates than structure free rivals. Forecasting skill stays comparable.
arxiv-2603-21180: Foo and Chang present ALMAB-DC, a framework for sequential experimental design with costly, gradient-free objectives. A Gaussian process surrogate with uncertainty aware sampling picks informative query points. A bandit controller splits evaluations across parallel workers, and an asynchronous scheduler handles uneven runtimes. On five benchmarks, the method beats standard designs on regret and matches a greedy benchmark on field estimation. It also lifts CIFAR-10 accuracy and cuts airfoil drag well below grid search.
arxiv-2603-21780: Holmgren and co-authors study additive functionals on split trees, random trees built by repeated splitting. Such functionals include node counts, leaf counts, and counts of small fringe subtrees. They also define fractional split trees, where the split vector need not sum to one. For their means, they prove convergence to a limit and give exact forms for some models. In some trees the spread is small next to the mean, giving a law of large numbers. In others the spread stays large, and a limit law takes over.
arxiv-2603-22480: Perera and co-authors map how technical debt shows up in serverless computing. They mine Stack Overflow, gathering near seventy-nine thousand serverless questions and labeling them with a deep learning model. About 37 percent turn out to be debt-related. The team sorts the debt into types and names six issues specific to serverless design. They also collect the fixes developers propose. The authors close by calling for tools that can spot such debt in serverless apps.
arxiv-2603-22680: Anwar and co-authors model how training load and rest shape injury risk in Thoroughbred racehorses. Bone injury is the most common such injury in these horses. The team extends a math model of bone adaptation and damage. They test many programs drawn from trainer practice in Victoria. Lower volume programs with high-speed work built adaptation with less damage. More frequent rests, at least twice a year, also cut damage. Longer rests of six weeks or more helped too. The model can guide safer training design.
arxiv-2603-22980: Damele extends a rigidity result for finite skew braces. Rump had shown that a finite skew brace with cyclic additive group has a solvable, almost Sylow cyclic multiplicative group. Damele proves the same when the additive group is a Z-group. Every such skew brace is also supersolvable, he shows. Its multiplicative group is 2-nilpotent as well. For odd-order braces, he proves the additive group is a Z-group exactly when the multiplicative group is one.
arxiv-2603-23280: Das and four co-authors rethink a key parameter of the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model. The soft-breaking term m12 squared is often treated as a mere knob that makes extra Higgs bosons heavy. The authors argue it encodes fresh symmetry breaking far above the electroweak scale. On that view, it and the electroweak vacuum value are two unrelated sources of the new scalars' masses. They define measures of how much mass comes from each source. Current diphoton data and resonance searches already limit those fractions.
arxiv-2603-23580: Sun and six co-authors present MetaKube, a Kubernetes failure diagnosis system that learns from past fixes. Older language model tools lean on fixed knowledge and never improve. MetaKube stores past resolutions as patterns in an episodic memory network. A meta-cognitive controller picks fast pattern matching or deep causal search by familiarity. Its local 8B model trains on 7,000 fault cases for privacy. On 1,873 real scenarios, scores jump from about 51 to over 90 points. Memory alone adds a clear share of that gain.
arxiv-2603-23980: Chakraborty studies how military spending shapes growth in an AK economy. He builds on a Keynesian goods-market model and splits state spending into civilian and military parts. Military outlays can lift demand and fund defense research. They also crowd out civilian investment and add rigidities. In his model, productivity depends on the degree of militarization, which makes the growth link nonlinear. Calibrated runs show moderate spending can aid growth for a time, while heavy militarization lowers long-run development. A two-country war simulation shows uneven costs.
arxiv-2603-24080: Saeed and Razniewski present LLMpedia, a framework that writes encyclopedia articles purely from a language model's memory. They generate about 1.3 million articles across three model families. Every claim is then checked against Wikipedia and curated web evidence. For gpt-5-mini, only 68.4 percent of claims on Wikipedia-covered topics verify as true, far below MMLU-style scores. Most of the gap comes from claims that cannot be verified, not from flat errors. All prompts, articles, and verdicts are released for inspection.
arxiv-2603-24280: Evers extends the Miquel-Steiner theorem to Cayley-Klein planes beyond the Euclidean case. In Euclidean geometry, the circumcircles of a quadrilateral's four triangles meet at one point. In Minkowski and Galilean planes, the statement needs a small change involving isotropic points. In elliptic, hyperbolic, and dual planes, the theorem fails in that form. A weaker version holds instead: the four circles share a common radical center. Evers also pins down the point more closely for special cases such as cyclic quadrilaterals.
arxiv-2603-24480: Zaher and co-authors present Positive-First Most Ambiguous, an active learning rule for finding rare classes in large unlabelled image sets. Standard active learning assumes balanced classes and large labelling budgets, which fails in skewed settings like wildlife work. Their rule picks samples near the class boundary, but favours likely positives. This speeds the finding of subtle visual classes while keeping each batch informative. In live search tests, it returns small batches with a high share of positives, unlike methods that oversample negatives.
arxiv-2603-24580: Mathur and co-authors study retrieval-augmented generation for question answering over AI policy documents. Their corpus, AGORA, holds 947 curated policy texts with dense legal language and overlapping rules. The system pairs a fine-tuned ColBERT retriever with a generator aligned by direct preference optimisation. Synthetic queries and pairwise preferences adapt both parts to the domain. Fine-tuning improves retrieval metrics, they find, but does not reliably improve end-to-end answers. Stronger retrieval can even yield more confident hallucinations when the needed document is absent from the corpus.
arxiv-2603-24880: Inoue and co-authors give a near-linear time four-colouring algorithm for planar graphs, improving the quadratic algorithm from 1996. Known proofs of the Four Colour Theorem cannot yield such an algorithm. They prove a stronger statement: every planar triangulation contains linearly many non-touching reducible configurations, or non-crossing obstructing cycles of length at most five. The discharging method finds reductions where combinatorial curvature is positive. Their work extends the search into large flat regions with zero curvature, opening routes to higher surfaces.
arxiv-2603-25080: Miao and co-authors build a telescope that reads both charge and place for fast atomic nuclei. The stack holds nine layers of silicon microstrip sensors with a wide active area and little material. A heavy ion beam test at CERN checked its performance. A hybrid learning method helps read charge from the strips. The system pins position to about a micron. Charge is read to better than 0.16 units for nuclei from hydrogen to copper. The team claims the sharpest joint charge and place readings yet for such a telescope.
arxiv-2603-25680: The CHIME Collaboration interprets its measurement of the 21 cm auto power spectrum near redshift one. The data span 608.2 to 707.8 MHz and a range of wavenumbers. One approach fits a parametric model to the spectrum. It bounds a combined amplitude of hydrogen density, bias, and redshift-space effects. Adding a prior on one factor breaks the tie between density and bias. A second approach compares the data with IllustrisTNG simulations. The authors report tension of 3.1 and 4.0 sigma with the two runs. They blame strong nonlinear clustering of hydrogen in the simulations.
arxiv-2603-25780: Yang shows that a judge agent can make AI-written scientific simulations far more reliable. Language models often write simulation code that fails in silence on hard problems. The judge applies classic checks: well-posedness, convergence, and error bounds. Across 134 test cases in 12 domains, silent failures fell from 42 percent to 1.5 percent. In a blind trial, 72 tasks from 12 outside scientists reached an 89 percent success rate with the judge. The rate without it was 53 percent. Yang also defines a spec format that makes problems machine-readable.
arxiv-2603-25980: Lim and co-authors present ASTRA, a method that finds transition states for chemical reactions without a guessed path. Transition states are saddle points that govern reaction rates and routes. ASTRA trains a diffusion model on known stable states. Guided sampling then aims at the surface between two basins. A score-aligned ascent step builds a reaction coordinate from score gaps. Physical forces push the search onto true saddle points. On tests from toy surfaces to biomolecules, ASTRA finds states with high precision. It also uncovers several rival pathways.
arxiv-2603-26680: Xiao and co-authors introduce AlpsBench, a benchmark for personalisation in language models built from real chats. Lifelong assistants must manage personal facts over time, yet past tests lean on synthetic dialogue. AlpsBench holds 2,500 long interaction sequences from WildChat, paired with human-checked structured memories. Four tasks cover extracting, updating, retrieving, and using personal facts across a memory's life. Frontier models struggle to spot hidden user traits, memory updates hit a ceiling, and recall drops sharply when distractor pools grow.
arxiv-2603-26880: Bisht and co-authors work out axion effective field theory in the BMHV renormalization scheme. That scheme treats the gamma-five matrix in a way that breaks naive Ward identities. Evanescent operators appear and feed into the identity violations. The authors derive bare and renormalized identities for chiral flavor currents. Diagram checks confirm the identities up to two loops in the strong coupling. They also find the finite renormalization that restores the four-dimensional identities. The result gives a consistent base for multi-loop axion calculations.
arxiv-2603-26980: Valente and co-authors extend the Caldeira-Leggett model to environments with thermal gradients. The standard model treats Brownian motion in a uniform-temperature bath. Heat gradients call for a richer environment description. The authors devise two generalized models and weigh each one's strengths and limits. Both models show signatures of thermophoresis, the drift of particles along a gradient. The framework could describe thermophoresis for quantum Brownian particles. That quantum case has stayed an open problem until now.
arxiv-2603-27280: Dutta and co-authors construct complete gauge models for a light axial gauge boson. The new boson couples only axially to quarks and leptons. Their construction starts from left-right symmetric universal seesaw models. An extra U(1) group supplies the axial gauge symmetry. Three versions, labeled A, B, and C, cancel anomalies in different ways. The models also accommodate small neutrino masses naturally. A new Dirac fermion linked through the portal can serve as dark matter. Model A even caps the gauge coupling through the Higgs charge assignment.
arxiv-2603-27580: Beckers and co-authors teach machines rolling dynamics without breaking physics rules. Wheeled systems must obey no-slip limits at all times. Standard learners can drift into impossible motions. Their Gaussian process uses a kernel built from the constraint set. Learned fields then satisfy the limits for every input. The kernel is shown to be valid and well posed. A rolling disk test shows the method works. Consistency of the learned model is also proven.
arxiv-2603-27680: Akhmetali and co-authors make supernova wave studies more realistic. Gravitational waves can reveal the dense-matter equation of state. Past learning studies used clean, simple setups. This work adds real detector noise. Four star models span twelve to forty solar masses. Spin rates range from slow to rapid. Bounce time is left unsure by up to twenty milliseconds. Classification accuracy holds up under all three changes. More training variety even helps scores.
arxiv-2603-27780: Siddiqui and co-authors test wave-particle duality under blurred causal order. The quantum switch superposes the order of two operations. They ask if one bound can join three coherence types. Spatial coherence, path marks, and causal coherence enter the test. Extremal switch states break any shared linear bound. One state maxes causal coherence while saturating spatial duality. Tracing out the order qubit restores the classic relation. Causal coherence names the hidden leftover part.
arxiv-2603-27880: Das treats the kernel itself as a moving object under MaxCal rules. A kernel encodes which distinctions an agent can draw. Path entropy maximization steers its change over time. Each kernel induces its own geometry on probability space. Fixed-point rules mark self-consistent kernels. Renormalization flow appears as a structured special case. Neural tangent kernel drift may fit the frame. Work bounds tie effort to new mutual information.
arxiv-2603-28580: The Euclid Collaboration reports 72 more galaxy-galaxy strong lenses from Euclid Quick Release 1 data. Earlier searches missed bright, low-redshift lenses because a Gaia-based pre-selection excluded some objects. Two searches found the new sample, one using machine learning plus expert checks and one using expert checks alone. The catalogue holds 38 grade A candidates and 34 grade B candidates. Detailed modelling confirms at least 41 of the 72 systems. Odd finds include edge-on disc lenses and red sources. The sample's median redshift is about 0.3 lower than the earlier sample.
arxiv-2603-29080: Chowers and co-authors ask whether the modality gap in multimodal models is a bug or a feature. Models like CLIP aim to align image and text embeddings in one space. Yet images and texts stay separated. They show that, under conditions, minimizing the contrastive loss yields a gap vector between the modalities. The gap is tied to robustness: shrinking it keeps clean accuracy but reduces output changes under perturbation. A post-processing step that moves one modality toward the other's mean raised robustness, with no accuracy loss.
arxiv-2603-29380: Kartikey and Bhatnagar give a finite-time analysis of multi-timescale stochastic optimization methods. They study two smoothed functional algorithms for simulation-based optimization. One is a two-timescale gradient method. The other is a three-timescale Newton method that estimates gradient and Hessian. Both use zeroth-order estimates. Earlier work showed only long-run convergence. They derive error bounds for the Hessian estimator and the gradient norms. Their step-size choices balance the main error terms. Experiments on the Mountain Car task support the theory.
arxiv-2603-29780: McDonald compares two versions of Peccei-Quinn inflation against new ACT data. One version is standard, with non-minimal coupling. The other adds Jordan frame terms that protect unitarity. With fast reheating, the second model lands within one sigma of ACT's spectral index value. The standard model sits more than two sigma below it. The safe model also allows much larger axion decay constants. For one case, its bound reaches 6.4 times ten to the thirteenth GeV.
arxiv-2603-29880: Eiter and co-authors prove convergence for a finite-volume scheme for Korteweg fluid systems. The scheme preserves key structure for Euler and Navier-Stokes variants. They show its solutions approach energy-variational solutions as the mesh refines. That solution concept is new for hyperbolic conservation laws. They extend it here to the Navier-Stokes-Korteweg model. Uniform estimates from the scheme drive the proof. Stability of the energy form under weak limits finishes it.
arxiv-2604-00180: Zhong, Zhou, Nie, and Tang study copositive optimization where the goal is a sparse polynomial and constraints are linear over the nonnegative orthant. They propose sparse Moment-SOS relaxations, prove when these relaxations are tight, and show tightness under a cop-SOS convexity assumption. Against dense versions, the sparse ones run faster. Tests confirm the speed gains.
arxiv-2604-00280: Misu and four colleagues show verifier pass rates mislead for LLM-made specifications: an always-true postcondition passes any verifier without saying anything about the code. They find 22.7 percent of verified specs lack postconditions, and verifier feedback repairs prompts without beating the best hand-written prompt. Their Spec-Harness rates behavioral adequacy on four axes: precondition and postcondition correctness and completeness, with Hoare-triple symbolic verification and mutation on built suites. As feedback, Spec-Harness lifts adequacy for agents and a CodeAct-style agent on held-out tests.
arxiv-2604-00580: Giottonini and Lemmin show that representation choice shapes what protein dynamics studies conclude. Atomic-scale runs give rich paths, but pulling robust, readable insight from huge data stays hard. Most studies lean on a single representation, yet that choice is not neutral. It reshapes fold shapes, likeness links, and seeming shifts drawn from the same run data. The authors add Orientation features, a spin-aware code for the protein backbone. They test it against common accounts across fast-folding proteins, large domain motions, and protein-protein binding.
arxiv-2604-01380: Zhang and colleagues derive a reduced model for rapidly spinning convection with uniform internal heating, where energy rules fail because the Coriolis force does no work. Their main result is proof of bounds on mean temperature and mean vertical convective heat transport. The bounds are in terms of Rayleigh and Ekman numbers, at infinite Prandtl number. The first quantity represents flow mixing, and the second heat-leaving asymmetry. They use alternative estimation techniques to previous studies and identify two distinct scaling behaviours for both quantities.
arxiv-2604-01480: Huang and colleagues present a self-evolving agentic framework for metasurface inverse design, coupling a coding agent, human-readable skill files, and a physics-based evaluator. Instead of changing model weights, it updates the skill files using solver feedback, leaving the base model and solver untouched. On a multi-type benchmark, same-type task success rises from 38 percent to 74 percent. Physical criteria met rise, and average attempts fall. On two new-type families, success stays near the top for one, and climbs from 0.20 to 0.90 for the other.
arxiv-2604-01680: Pan and colleagues propose MIP, joining an LLM, a compiler, and code utilities for implicit inconsistencies in patch porting. Current approaches mostly cope with inconsistencies visible near a patch, but falter on ones needing cross-codebase mapping knowledge. MIP uses different strategies: when source names exist in the target codebase, it uses compiler reports; otherwise, it retrieves code segment pairs across codebases as mapping knowledge. In cross-fork and cross-branch trials, MIP clears over double the patches of the top baseline.
arxiv-2604-01880: Cirrincione builds DDCL-INCRT, a transformer that designs its own shape during training. Transformers are chosen too big, with heads and layers removable with no loss. Deep Dual Competitive Learning swaps the feedforward block for prototype vectors marking key data paths. Incremental Transformer starts with one head, adding another only when missed information passes a threshold. The two boost each other: each head widens prototype spread, raising the trigger for the next, settling into a hierarchy. That hierarchy is proved unique and minimal, with stability and convergence guaranteed.
arxiv-2604-02280: Fofadiya and Tiwari tackle memory bloat in long chat agents. Unchecked memory growth causes decay and false memory spread, with tests showing steep drops across stages. Their budgeted forgetting frame scores memories by recency, frequency and meaning fit, pruning under a fixed cap. Tests show long horizon F1 above a 0.583 baseline, steadier recall and fewer false memories, all without growing context use.
arxiv-2604-02380: Maignant, Conrad and von Tycowicz infer single cell differentiation trees from RNA velocity fields with VeloTree. Path distance between cells is estimated from cell similarities, but RNA velocity adds a vector field of expression change per gene. Their cell dissimilarity measure, the squared varifold distance between integral curves of the velocity field, robustly estimates path distance on the target tree. Preprocessing and integration routines precede the measure, and tests on simulated and real datasets recover trees with high accuracy against state of the art rivals.
arxiv-2604-02480: Das extends a geometric framework for measuring what neural networks can express, moving it from braid patterns to discriminantal patterns. She describes compatible piecewise linear functions, which are functions built from flat pieces, through circuit relations and a matroid account based on Mobius inversion. The dimension equals the count of independent sets, and for circuits of size three the functions are fixed by values on subsets of at most two elements.
arxiv-2604-02780: Gao and three colleagues offer a unified view of adversarial membership manipulation in vision models. The work is the first unified look at this phenomenon. Tiny perturbations move images from outside the member region into it in membership inference attacks, breaking the honest-query premise of existing attacks. The trick works across architectures and datasets. The attacks studied target vision models only. A gradient-norm collapse trajectory separates faked from true members despite near-identical meanings, grounding a sound detection plan. The defense builds on geometry, not on semantics.
arxiv-2604-02880: Chen and seven colleagues introduce InstructTable, an instruction-guided framework for table structure recognition from images, a task strained by merged and empty cells. Visual-only models lack semantic support, while vision-language models underplay visual structure. Table instruction pre-training directs attention to fine-grained structural patterns, complementary fine-tuning preserves robust visual modeling, and a template-free Table Mix Expand method synthesizes large-scale authentic tabular data.
arxiv-2604-03180: Douglas, Balci, and Aylett-Bullock build PRISM, a topic-modeling method that distills sparse language-model labels into a lightweight sentence encoder. Thresholded clustering then splits the embedding space into fine topics, even separating close topics inside narrow domains. Across corpora, PRISM beats leading local models and large frontier embeddings while needing only a few language-model queries to train.
arxiv-2604-03280: Hasan and colleagues build urban food-delivery networks that stay robust without the cost of fully connected graphs. Their UMST method unions several minimum spanning trees made through random edge changes, keeping many alternative routes between hotspots with far fewer edges. Across United States cities, it uses 20 to 40 times fewer edges than full graphs while reaching 88 to 96 percent delivery success without any training.
arxiv-2604-03480: Ismayilzada and colleagues measure how language models align with human brain activity during creative thinking, using fMRI from 170 people doing the Alternate Uses Task. Alignment rises with model size in the default mode network and with idea originality in both networks studied, clearest early in the creative process. Post-training objectives shift alignment selectively: creativity tuning preserves high-creativity alignment, while reasoning training reverses the pattern.
arxiv-2604-03580: Oyama and colleagues show with atom models that slow motion in supercooled liquids fits a zero-temperature avalanche criticality picture. That picture covers structural settling and dynamical heterogeneity. That finding points to the energy landscape as key, so they measure that landscape from three angles. Their energy-landscape picture explains earlier puzzling observations near the mode-coupling transition. These include capped dynamical susceptibility and trapped wobbly modes in saddle shapes.
arxiv-2604-03680: Kerstin Jordaan and Vikash Kumar studied when adding one natural extra point makes the roots of two polynomial families line up in strict alternation. They looked at linked recurrence rules that force the roots of a shifted polynomial to alternate with a second family. They also set out the conditions on the extra point that yield full alternation. The approach gathers many scattered results into one frame. It gives new cases for Krawtchouk, Meixner, and Narayana polynomials, plus fresh proofs for Jacobi and Laguerre families.
arxiv-2604-03780: Adrien Cances and colleagues showed that a class of smoothed transport problems can be tracked by ordinary differential equations in the smoothing parameter. Starting values for fully smoothed problems are usually known outright. Solving the equations then recovers answers for any smoothing level, and the limit gives the unsmoothed answer. The team proved the same pattern for a variant with an unscaled extra term. They used standard ODE solvers to beat Newton-style methods on examples.
arxiv-2604-04180: Alex Fedoseyev developed an analytical framework for turbulent channel flow from the Alexeev flow equations. Mean streamwise velocity combines a laminar parabolic part with a nonlinear turbulent part, matching channel and pipe data from Reynolds numbers 3,000 to 35,000,000. Gaps run about 1 percent at moderate values and 3 percent at the highest. The transverse velocity analysis yields expressions for its main spatial structure. Coupling the two reveals kink-type solutions, sharp local transitions read as streamwise streak patterns, and a unified account of mean shapes, secondary flows, and streak formation.
arxiv-2604-04480: Illi and Qaraqe propose a beyond-diagonal RIS-aided ISAC scheme for multi-user networks. A dual-functional base station serves downlink users while sensing eavesdropping targets. The team formulates an optimization maximizing per-target reflected powers under secrecy and power constraints. An alternating optimization algorithm solves it. It gives a local optimum for the BD-RIS scattering, beamforming and noise covariance matrices. Results show sensing gains over the diagonal RIS baseline and an improved secrecy-sensing trade-off, with rising secrecy and little reflected-power loss.
arxiv-2604-04680: Nguyen and three colleagues show that a duplication of hypercharge, identical for the normal sector but different for the dark sector, may manifestly address neutrino mass and dark matter. The twin hypercharge setup keeps the normal sector's hypercharge unchanged while giving the dark sector a different hypercharge. This split, the authors show, manifestly addresses two open problems at once: the origin of neutrino mass and the nature of dark matter.
arxiv-2604-04780: Hao and eight colleagues present CLEAR, a framework that lets multimodal models use their generative power on degraded images. Blur, noise, compression, and dim light wreck understanding, yet training never asks models to generate while reasoning. The decode then reencode path also blocks joint tuning. CLEAR fine-tunes on a degradation set to set a generate then answer pattern. It then bridges generation and reasoning with a link, and tunes text and image with reinforcement learning. Tests on MMD-Bench show robustness on degraded inputs with clean skill intact.
arxiv-2604-04980: Kedia, Messerich, and Landgraf introduce COMB, a compact open modular robotic platform for experiments inside honeybee colonies. Working in a hive demands tight fits, tolerance for fouling and hive conditions, and sensing plus local action. COMB fits observation-hive frames. It integrates an XY positioning stage, a Movable Access Window for sealed tool access through the hive wall, interchangeable payload modules, and embedded control for repeatable trajectories and signals. Its abilities are shown through three modules, including a biomimetic dance-and-signaling payload and a comb scanner.
arxiv-2604-05180: Liu and Alaniz give MIRAGE, a tool for precise local editing when images contain multiple similar cases needing single edits. Models suffer over-editing and mix-ups with multiple same cases and mixed orders. MIRAGE parses orders into local subsets with a model, then uses joint cleaning, adding codes of target regions into the space while keeping background wholeness through a path. Tests on MIRA-Bench and RefEdit-Bench show it beats old methods on precise changes while keeping backgrounds steady.
arxiv-2604-05380: Sundar and three colleagues push quantum chemistry toward excited-state calculations, where bond-breaking strains classical methods and new hardware. They combine ground-state routines with q-sc-EOM, a subspace method for excited states. Davidson routines and basis-rotation grouping tame its measurement cost, cutting the scaling from a twelfth power to a fifth power in system size. Run on hardware with readout-error mitigation and symmetry projection, the method gives excited-state energies close to the mark, with gate noise the main error.
arxiv-2604-05880: Goswami models dense crowds shifting from stuck states to boundary-led peeling and migration. Particles carry spatial spots plus a scalar inner state, with crowding-linked mobilities cross-coupled between coordinates. Tuning inner-state spread alone drives the shift, with broad excursions, outward bias, and edge-localized activity growing with system size.
arxiv-2604-06380: Barone and eight colleagues report student projects from the 2026 ESO La Silla Observing School. Six students studied binary stars with HARPS and EFOSC2. One subgroup used HARPS on the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect, finding HD 115264 well aligned, likely from strong tides. Another subgroup studied blue stragglers in open clusters, checking abundances and membership with HARPS and radial velocities with EFOSC2. For Rediet, they found radial velocity shifts from second overtone pulsation, confirming delta Scuti character. One student imaged planetary nebulae and proved one central star binary, confirming earlier ZTF estimates.
arxiv-2604-06580: Siqueira and Monteiro Ribeiro ask which traits shape how software engineers judge company training. They surveyed 282 Brazilian engineers, crossing 27 survey items with nine background traits, and found only 35 of 243 links significant. Whether training was required mattered most, shifting 24 of 27 items. Experience showed a low-engagement zone between three and six years, and senior technical staff reported a gap in soft-skills training, while personal traits and firm size mattered little.
arxiv-2604-06780: Byun and Kim prove Calderón-Zygmund estimates for generalized double phase equations with matrix weights. The operator joins a patchy elliptic double phase form with a degenerate or singular matrix weight under a small log-BMO condition. Under set assumptions, higher integrability of the weighted datum yields higher integrability of the weighted gradient of weak solutions. The work unifies double phase theory and weighted elliptic theory, showing how Orlicz growth meets matrix weights.
arxiv-2604-07080: Braun, Poncet, Morin, and Bartolo study arrays of tiny spinning motors that arrange their own motion with no set plan. Most work on self run swarms has chased forward drive, while spin as a design route has drawn far less care. The team built sheets of thousands of small printed rotary motors linked by springs and watched how their spin settled. Motors that spin in free directions fell into a neat alternating pattern, then showed shared timing, and built in flaws set off free waves of timing.
arxiv-2604-07380: Xu follows the spectral edge, the top direction of parameter-update grams, through grokking in two sequence tasks. Before grokking, the edge is driven by gradients and does real work. At grokking, gradient and weight decay line up, and the edge turns into a compression axis. It is flat to nudges yet vital to remove, over 4000 times more potent than random directions. Three broad classes emerge, forecast by a gap-flow equation, and nonlinear probes show facts are re-encoded, not lost.
arxiv-2604-07480: Shehab, Aspeel, and Ozay learn reward machines, automaton-like structures capturing the memory needed for multi-stage tasks, directly from raw state trajectories. Hand-specifying a reward machine plus its labeling function is daunting, and prior work assumes access to reward, label, or node observations. This paper assumes none of those, showing what trajectory data suffices to learn the machine in this information-scarce regime. The result extends to active learning, where trajectory extensions are queried incrementally to improve data and computational efficiency. Grid-world examples demonstrate the approach.
arxiv-2604-07980: Huang presents an object-centric stereo ranging system for autonomous driving, focused on long-range highway vehicle detection. Dense stereo matching methods like block matching and semi-global matching produce per-pixel disparity maps but cost heavily, react to lighting differences, and lose accuracy at long range where disparities shrink. The system unifies depth approaches, dense disparity, object-centric Census-based template matching, and monocular geometric priors, in one detection-ranging-tracking pipeline. A novel Census-based template matching algorithm with GPU acceleration forms the key contribution.
arxiv-2604-08080: Ye and Wong study optimal switching over finite horizons, with set intervention dates and continuous-time observations between decisions. They build a dual deep-learning framework yielding computable upper bounds. A dual representation for multiple switching comes from martingale penalties, with the smallest given by Doob martingales of continuation values, so the upper bound is fully known. They carry DeepMartingale from optimal stopping to optimal switching, proving convergence for the upper-bound loss and an L2-surrogate loss. An expressivity analysis follows under the stated structural assumptions.
arxiv-2604-08380: van Luijk and Wilming clarify how families of quantum states convert into one another under positive trace preserving maps. They show Neyman Pearson tests generate the smallest sufficient Jordan algebra, extending the Koashi Imoto picture to this wider setting. Equality in data processing bounds then still yields a recovery map, and two simple tests convert under these maps exactly when they convert under decomposable trace preserving maps.
arxiv-2604-08780: Mohamad Danesh and seven colleagues build a four legged world model keyed to body shape for cross body walking. Motion models trained on one robot fail on another. Their QWM keys a single motion model on scale free real traits via a body shape encoder, tuning reward balancer, and latent keying, training policies fully offline. A model free policy matches QWM on training robots but weakens on unseen ones. QWM transfers zero shot to new four legged robots without fine tuning.
arxiv-2604-08880: Kajitsuka, Honda, and Takase revisit the size gap in chain of thought teaching from a hands on view. Teaching moves thinking from a big teacher to a small student, but earlier work reports failure when the skill mismatch is large. The authors find teaching often harms the student below its pre teaching start, and that some prior settings, while good for proving the effect, miss real use. Under more real settings the gap does not always rule, and stronger teachers tend to win when options differ a lot in scores.
arxiv-2604-08980: Luo and three colleagues propose the Neighbourhood Transformer, a graph neural network built for graphs where linked nodes differ, not for graphs where neighbours resemble each other. Standard graph networks lean on a homophily assumption, the idea that connected nodes are alike, which fails on heterophilic graphs. Drawing on the newly found monophily property of real graphs, the model adds switchable attention that adapts to each neighbourhood. Tests on ten real datasets, five heterophilic and five homophilic, show it beating all leading methods on node classification.
arxiv-2604-09280: Hénique and colleagues build AMO-ENE, a model that blends many data types to predict outcomes in HPV-linked throat cancer with extranodal extension. That spread beyond nodes is a new warning sign left out of staging, hindered by uneven outlining, low node contrast on CT, and slow hand labeling. Their auto pipeline outlines nodal extension from treatment CT scans, extracts image and deep features, and grades seen extension. Combined with main tumor features, it predicts outcomes in 397 patients, reaching 88 percent AUC for metastatic recurrence at two years.
arxiv-2604-09480: Zhou and five colleagues present Online3R, online learning for steady step-by-step rebuilding. Online3R adapts to new scenes through online learning, fixing mismatch problems in step-by-step rebuilding. Learnable lightweight visual prompts enter a frozen geometry base model. They capture new scene knowledge while keeping geometry prediction skill, and a local-global self-taught plan enforces matching rules at test time. Local rules use fused results for pseudo ground truth, global rules use sparse keyframes, and tests show Online3R beats previous best methods.
arxiv-2604-09780: Wang and two co-authors argue that expert specialization in mixture-of-experts emerges from representation space, not routing. Since routers are linear maps, hidden-state similarity explains expert-usage similarity. The team confirms this at token and sequence level across five models. They show a load-balancing loss damps directions shared across hidden states, keeping routing varied, which explains specialization collapse on narrow data. Despite this clean account, specialization patterns resist human interpretation: expert overlap for the same question runs no higher than for different questions, at about 60 percent.
arxiv-2604-09880: Panova reviews NA61/SHINE, a fixed-target experiment at the CERN SPS studying the onset of deconfinement and strong-force matter. The team scanned collision energy and system size, from proton-proton to lead-lead crashes, measuring hadron spectra in nucleus-nucleus crashes. New results cover charged hadrons in central xenon-lanthanum crashes and baryons in central argon-scandium crashes. The kaon-to-pion ratio and proton spectra, set against NA49 lead-lead data, trace how baryon-number transport shifts with energy and system size.
arxiv-2604-10080: Archey, Buck, Mohammadkarimi, Phillips, and Seth establish comparison and divisibility for crossed product C*-algebras. They cover automorphisms of C(X, D) over minimal homeomorphisms. They also cover compact group actions with finite Rokhlin dimension and commuting towers, and actions with restricted tracial Rokhlin property plus comparison. They deduce these crossed products are pure, with stable rank one and at times real rank zero. They give examples where these properties defy earlier results, whether D lacks Z-stability, the spaces are not finite dimensional, or both.
arxiv-2604-10280: Suzuki, Chiba, Wyse, and Horigome map the Milky Way stellar halo within 70 kiloparsecs of the Sun from Hyper Suprime-Cam imaging. Using turn-off stars as distance tracers, they build a forward model accounting for distance errors, the solar position, and limited sky coverage. The smooth halo follows a double power-law profile with a break radius of 17.4 kpc, inner slope about minus 3, and outer slope about minus 5. The steep outer slope points to early massive accretion events, like Gaia Enceladus and the Sausage.
arxiv-2604-10380: Chakraborti, Zhang, Peng, Mao, and Reiter let ATMs hand out digital coins with no bank link. In most digital cash plans, the bank must sign each withdrawal, so a dead link blocks users. Their bearer tokens keep spending private, unforgeable, and untraceable by outsiders. A one time voucher moves coins from machine to user while hiding both sides from others. The design builds on compact digital cash work from Camenisch and colleagues in 2005.
arxiv-2604-10580: Turetzky, Dekel, Aronowitz, Hoory, and Adi test stress placement in synthetic speech. One sentence can correct, contrast, or clarify based on which word bears stress. Their CAST set pairs twin sentences with contexts that demand distinct stressed words. Text only models read the right stress from context with ease. Speech systems, though, often fail to sound it, a gap the new set exposes.
arxiv-2604-10880: Zhang, Liu, and Wei propose two hyperfusion schemes for larger hyperentangled W states. One fuses n-photon and m-photon hyper-W states into an (n+m-2)-photon state; another fuses n-, m-, and t-photon states into an (n+m+t-3)-photon state. Both use polarizing beam splitters, balanced beam splitters, half-wave plates, single-photon detectors, and cross-Kerr nonlinearities, with no conditional gates, path couplers, or ancillary photons. The fused states stay hyperentangled in polarization and spatial degrees of freedom, and a garbage output state signals efficiency.
arxiv-2604-11080: Kim and five colleagues propose ReSpinQuant, a quantization system for language models using layer-wise residual subspace rotation. Rotation-based post-training cuts signal outliers. Global methods fuse rotations into attention and feed-forward blocks for speed. They suffer limited power from a single learned rotation matrix across all layers. Layer-wise methods achieve better scores through local tuning but cannot fuse rotations into weights, needing online math with large cost. It fixes this cost through offline rotation fusion and basis match using leftover subspace rotation.
arxiv-2604-11380: Seo builds an end-to-end differentiable network traffic simulator with dynamic route choice. Gradients then come from automatic differentiation, not manual adjoint derivations or slow numerical methods. A link transmission model with min-max operations has subgradients almost everywhere. Dynamic route choice yields continuous diverge ratios at nodes. On the Chicago-Sketch network, with about 2500 links, one million vehicles, and 15000 decision variables, a dynamic congestion toll optimization reached a high-quality solution in 3000 iterations in about 40 minutes. The code, named UNsim, is open source.
arxiv-2604-11980: Cordeiro, Pacifico, and Zhang introduce mean dimension and metric mean dimension for general iterated function systems, setting out basic traits of these measures. They prove the mean value always sits below both the lower and upper metric values in this setting. Systems with the small edge trait have zero mean value. Finally, they add a gluing orbit trait and prove it ensures above-zero topological entropy under suitable linking and non-stiffness terms.
arxiv-2604-12380: Hao Wang and six colleagues build a prompt method for finding camouflaged objects. Such objects blend into their surroundings, frustrating ordinary detectors. Their framework serves the Segment Anything Model with prompts from any extra sensing channel. Depth, heat, and polarization images all feed the same shared prompts. A light refinement step then sharpens rough masks. Tests on three benchmarks show stronger and more general detection.
arxiv-2604-12480: Mahmoud Fakhry and two colleagues separate audio sources in echoing rooms. Gaussian models describe mixtures through source spectra and spatial covariances. Parameters are usually fit by likelihood maximization. Their method instead uses nonnegative factorization with prior variance knowledge. Spectral bases come from a trained library or direct extraction. Tensor factorization then picks bases that best match observed power spectra. Sparsity, tuned through beta, drives separation quality more than beta's training value. Tests show better separation than rival methods.
arxiv-2604-12980: Juan Hernandez and Mikhail Khramtsov link black hole state counting to the Page curve. Semiclassical gravity path integrals explain quantum traits of gravity. Bekenstein-Hawking entropy counts black hole microstates. Hawking radiation entanglement follows the Page curve, matching unitarity. The two questions prove equivalent through the gravity path integral. Any complete microstate basis matching black hole entropy resolves information loss automatically. A convex optimization problem for radiation entropy connects the two questions.
arxiv-2604-13280: Pham and 24 colleagues pin down traits of peaks in neon-19 that govern the fluorine-18 proton-alpha oxygen-15 reaction rate and fluorine-18 production in novae. That production is key to the 511-keV positron-annihilation line. Measuring alpha and proton angular distributions from states made in the fluorine-19 helium-3 tritium neon-19 reaction, they spot six near-threshold proton s-wave fluorine-18-plus-proton states. Tail scaling of these states was studied with the symmetry-adapted no-core shell model, and earlier studies much underestimated the errors.
arxiv-2604-13380: Focsan and seven colleagues test whether the TalkMoves codebook, built for whole-classroom talk, transfers to one-on-one tutoring across chat, audio, and multimodal sessions. Two raters with decades of classroom experience applied TalkMoves and a hybrid AI-human codebook to six sessions. TalkMoves achieved higher inter-rater reliability, while the hybrid codebook covered more moves and felt easier to use. Both missed tutoring-specific moves and blurred actions shown only through nonverbal or multimodal cues.
arxiv-2604-13580: Li and three colleagues measure what Japan's KAGRA detector adds to gravitational-wave sky maps for merging neutron stars. Using injected signals and a coherence-based mapping method, they find that even at its present modest reach, KAGRA sharpens locations by breaking geometric ambiguities with new baselines. As its sensitivity grows, localization areas shrink further, and a range near 30 megaparsecs marks a practical benchmark for follow-up with telescopes.
arxiv-2604-13780: Mahajan and Seymour develop Soft Q(lambda) for entropy-regularised reinforcement learning. It is a multi-step, off-policy method using eligibility traces. Soft Q-learning optimizes returns plus a penalty for diverging from a reference policy. Its multi-step extensions were limited to on-policy sampling under the Boltzmann policy. The authors give an n-step formulation, extend it fully off-policy with a new Soft Tree Backup operator, and unify both into an online trace framework for credit assignment under arbitrary behavior policies.
arxiv-2604-14080: Zhang, Labrosse, and Mulay study how prominence plasma traits shape the helium-II 304-angstrom line during a February 2022 eruption seen by Solar Orbiter EUI camera. After fixing temperature, radial speed, and altitude, they compute 200 random models and display them in parallel plots. Column mass and temperature steepness emerge as key drivers. Radiation dominates line formation.
arxiv-2604-14280: Stoiber and three colleagues trace how a satellite galaxy's orbit decides whether its stars form a stream or a shell system. Using the Magneticum Pathfinder simulation, they follow a stream and a shell system from progenitor to host, comparing stellar distributions with starting positions. The stream progenitor orbits more circularly, and stream stars from varied starting radii land at roughly equal host distances. The visible stream shows only core stars, while shell stars keep their radial order, with inner stars staying nearer the host center.
arxiv-2604-14980: Banerjee, Sayin, Teso, and Passerini address hybrid decision making where humans keep final decisions and AI supplies guidance. Existing learning-to-guide approaches compound information about all possible outcomes, making guidance hard to digest. Their ConfGuide approach uses conformal risk control to select outcome sets, capping the false negative rate for more succinct, targeted guidance. Tests on a real-world multi-label medical diagnosis task show promise for the approach.
arxiv-2604-15180: Gonçalves and colleagues speed up sparse attention with AdaSplash-2, a faster differentiable alternative to softmax. The bottleneck is computing the normalizer for alpha-entmax attention, which has lagged softmax despite input-dependent sparsity. A histogram of attention scores, built on the fly and stored in on-chip SRAM, seeds the normalizer so it typically converges in one or two iterations. With a sparsity-aware GPU build that skips zero blocks cheaply, it keeps pace with softmax at short contexts and gains at long ones.
arxiv-2604-15280: Agarwal and three colleagues investigate why vision-language models, strong on many visual tasks, still lag specialist classifiers at reading human emotion from faces. They blame two flaws: skewed training data that collapses rare emotions into common ones, and sparse frame sampling that misses micro-expressions lasting a quarter to half a second. Their fix turns in-between frames into text summaries fed beside keyframes, preserving the emotional arc.
arxiv-2604-15680: Liu and four colleagues map big antenna links at FR3 bands of 8 and 15 gigahertz with the same dish size, using a two-band sounder in city macro cells. High bands show thin delay and space links, and 15 gigahertz still trails by near 3.0 decibels at cell rims even with four times the parts. Yet more parts beat the thin links for speed, with data rates well past the 8 gigahertz band.
arxiv-2604-15780: Si, Li, Backes, and Zhang prune the unsafe bits of LLMs, cutting bad outputs while keeping skill, with a touch that needs just modest GPU gear. A no-gradient credit rule finds the weights tied to unsafe acts, works across builds and squeezed variants, and beats jailbreak tricks while barely denting skill. In lottery-ticket terms, models hold unsafe tickets that spark harm, and pruning bares safety tickets that hold skill while lining up outputs. This gives a cheap late fix for thin setups.
arxiv-2604-16180: Li and Song report running a data-driven chaos indicator live on the NSLS-II storage ring, using turn-by-turn beam position data to judge how predictable electron motion is. A stand-in model of the one-turn map is trained first, and its out-of-sample uncertainty serves as the chaos measure. Tuning sextupole magnets against nonlinear effects then widens the dynamic aperture clearly and improves injection efficiency.
arxiv-2604-16480: Lin and colleagues mount a stereo-vision drone system to locate radiata pine branches that need pruning. The pipeline segments branches, comparing YOLOv8, YOLOv9 and Mask R-CNN variants on 71 image pairs from a ZED Mini camera, then estimates depth. A classic method and several deep stereo methods were tested, with centroid triangulation and outlier rejection to compute branch distance. At one to two metres, deep disparity maps gave more coherent depth than the classic method, showing that low-cost stereo vision can support automated branch positioning.
arxiv-2604-16680: Haitman and colleagues open C-GenReg, a free framework for 3D point cloud registration. Matching struggles across sensing modalities, sampling gaps and scenes. C-GenReg moves matching into an image domain, where a world model makes matching RGB views from input shapes. A base model finds dense correspondences from made views, lifted back to 3D through depth maps. A Match-then-Fuse scheme combines made-RGB and raw geometric scores, keeping each mode bias. All modules are pretrained and run without fine-tuning, making the system zero-shot and ready.
arxiv-2604-16880: Jin and three colleagues address a timing flaw in ring-based collective operations, the workhorse pattern for distributed AI training. Network jitter leaves some steps ahead of others and drags out completion. Their in-network Symphony design tracks each job's pipeline progress and throttles racing flows so laggards catch up, cutting communication time by up to 54 percent in simulation.
arxiv-2604-16980: Bassett and ten colleagues evaluate ten multimodal language models on 539 real inpatient cases from a tertiary public hospital in South Africa. Radiology images and reports, lab results, notes, and vital signs feed the models, while expert panels set ground truth for 300 cases and a three-model jury scores every output. Models cluster tightly, beat routine ward diagnoses on average safety and accuracy, and GPT-5.1 leads, with low-cost models nearly matching top ones.
arxiv-2604-17080: Micheli and Papikian study the dimension of isogeny spaces between supersingular Drinfeld modules of rank at least two. By treating homomorphisms as a normed lattice in a local division algebra and analyzing successive minima, they obtain an exact closed-form dimension formula valid for every bound. Structural constraints then imply a stabilization formula for large bounds, with a conjectured sharper threshold proved for rank two via automorphic methods.
arxiv-2604-17180: Ang and five colleagues present BranchBench, a benchmark for branchable databases under agentic exploration. They characterize five workloads — agentic software engineering, failure reproduction, data curation, MCTS, and simulation — and build macrobenchmarks around branch-mutate-evaluate loops plus microbenchmarks of lifecycle costs. Evaluating Neon, DoltgreSQL, Tiger Data, Xata, and PostgreSQL baselines, they find a tension. Systems tuned for fast branching suffer reads up to 5-4000x slower as branches deepen, while systems tuned for fast operations incur creation and switching latency 25-1500x higher. No system supports the workloads at scale.
arxiv-2604-17280: Bai and Fang study the Fučik spectrum, the pairs of weights for which a weighted operator equation on all of space admits a nonzero solution. They prove a first nontrivial curve of that spectrum exists and trace its shape, including steady decline and limiting behavior, despite estimates from bounded regions failing here. As an application, they show the related nonlinear equation gains multiple solutions, extending spectral theory to operators whose weight grows fast.
arxiv-2604-17480: Bench examines trustworthy domain adaptation for wearable photoplethysmography, the light-based pulse signal in watches and sensors. Deep generative models can align test features with a classifier's training data, but their hallucinations may degrade predictions. Standard uncertainty checks lack ground truth for made-up data and ignore how outputs will be used downstream. A decision-based uncertainty method answers both concerns, and a pulse-denoising case study for atrial fibrillation shows how it judges made-up outputs by downstream value.
arxiv-2604-17580: Xie calculates the Witt ring of the real sphere. A Witt ring gathers the quadratic forms over a space into an algebraic structure, recording how forms add and multiply up to equivalence. Computing it for the sphere pins down that structure for one of geometry's most basic objects. The paper delivers the calculation itself, a concise algebraic result for readers working with quadratic forms and the topology of spheres.
arxiv-2604-17780: Nam and Ahn investigate phi decay to pi+ pi- pi0 with rho-pi mechanism, direct three-pion term, and constant background. Resonance uses the Gounaris-Sakurai propagator, neutral channels include rho0-omega mixing, and pi-pi interaction enters through the Omnes function. Omnes factors apply per subsystem, direct amplitude takes an averaged factor, and bare coupling avoids double-counting. Theoretical width is 0.6915 MeV, above empirical 0.660 plus-or-minus 0.020 MeV, with direct weight 8.393e-3 and resonant weight 0.9619. Dalitz plots show three-band structure.
arxiv-2604-18180: Wang revisits Albert Einstein's 1925 paper on Bose-Einstein condensation through its English translation. He walks readers through Einstein's calculations for specific heat above the condensation temperature. Along the way he corrects some numerical errors and compares Einstein's formula with a different one published in 2004. A short history of how Einstein's theory gained acceptance rounds out the comment.
arxiv-2604-18480: Goodearl and Letzter study when division algebras count as affine, meaning generated from a finite list over a central subfield. Amitsur proved in 1956 that over fields too big to count, such objects must be algebraic over the field. The authors extend the question to common examples over any fields, above all fractions of stacked skew polynomial rings. Many transcendental examples prove nonaffine, while Weyl systems and quantum affine spaces prove affine exactly when finite-dimensional over their centers.
arxiv-2604-18580: Horbatko proposes Sessa, a decoder placing attention inside a recurrent feedback path for long context modeling. In Transformers, attention reaches any element but dilutes token influence when diffuse, while state models can lose long range sensitivity unless information stays. Sessa creates many attention paths for past tokens to influence later states, rather than a single attention read or recurrent chain. Under assumptions, Sessa has power law memory tails with slower decay than Transformer and Mamba baselines, and leads on long context benchmarks while staying competitive on short contexts.
arxiv-2604-18680: Karikos and three colleagues extend a classic continued-fraction technique for black-hole ringdown beyond the cases it was built for. Their reduction scheme turns longer recurrence relations, which arise in modified gravity and non-Kerr spacetimes, into the three-term form the method requires. They test it on slowly rotating black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity, matching independent calculations for the main ringing mode.
arxiv-2604-18780: Johnson and four colleagues present Flash-SemiCRF, a fused kernel for exact semi Markov conditional random field inference on large problems. Semi CRFs label segments of a sequence, not individual positions, but existing implementations must store an edge tensor that grows with length, segment length, and label count. Flash-SemiCRF replaces the stored tensor with prefix sum lookup, uses a streaming forward backward pass with checkpoint normalization, and controls drift with zero centered cumulative scores. Working memory stays sublinear while exact gradients are preserved.
arxiv-2604-19080: Zhou and ten colleagues find optical excitation of a WS2 and CGT bilayer produces an opposite torque to an isolated film. Typical pump pulses heat the magnet into precession, but charge transfer across the interface alters anisotropy and makes triggering torque. Time resolved Kerr data plus density functional and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert simulations support this mechanism. The result opens ultrafast control of magnetization in layered magnets with type-II band offsets. Spin currents into the magnetic layer can also trigger precession.
arxiv-2604-19280: Ciccarelli and Fatibene carry out a canonical analysis of the Holst model of general relativity, setting the Barbero parameter to zero and leaving lapse and shift functions unconstrained. That choice matters because it stays viable in all dimensions, laying groundwork for extending loop quantum gravity beyond three space and one time dimension. Through field decomposition and projection, they derive 37 equations matching the 37 field components to be found. Leaving the gauge unfixed also exposes three equations that are normally satisfied identically as genuine differential constraints.
arxiv-2604-19480: Baltacı, Loiseau, and Aubry analyze deep sprite-based image models, which break image collections into recurrent patterns. Foundation models advance segmentation fast, and diffusion algorithms compose more realistic images, yet spotting repeat patterns across a collection remains open. Sprite-based models show promise for clustering and decomposition and appeal through high clarity. But they come in varied forms, need tailoring to specific datasets, and struggle with many-object images. The authors dissect their design, name core components, test them on clustering benchmarks, and propose a deep sprite-based method.
arxiv-2604-19680: Fan and five colleagues present IR-Flow, an image restoration method built on rectified flow that bridges single-step discriminative mapping and multi-step generative sampling. Single-step mappings often lose fine detail through expectation learning, while generative approaches waste effort on many sampling steps and tangle noise with leftover error. IR-Flow builds multilevel data flows that span varied damage levels, then learns cumulative velocity fields that steer intermediate states toward the clean target.
arxiv-2604-19880: Brdar and Mir test whether future tau neutrino detectors can probe Lorentz invariance, the rule that physics is the same at all speeds and in all directions. A breach would shift the flavor mix of high-energy cosmic neutrinos seen by GRAND and POEMMA. Their projected limits beat past low-energy tests by orders of magnitude for single breaches. When several breaches act at once, the limits shift a lot, so joint cases need care.
arxiv-2604-20180: Watanabe, Sels, and Tindall use a flat tensor net set up to run change based quantum routines on flat qubit grids. They test QAOA on Ising spin glass tasks over heavy hex and square grids. Settings tuned on small cases and moved to far bigger cases help only to mid depths, showing a cap on setting focus. Tuning on bigger cases at once dodges low spots and yields lower energy samples, with old style run costs staying tame at mid bond size.
arxiv-2604-20480: The MAGIC Collaboration examines the January 2010 flare of Mrk 421, a blazar bright before its February outburst. Fitting multi-wavelength spectra with JetSeT, the team tests a leptonic log-parabola model with a low-energy power-law branch. It also tests pile-up shapes predicted by stochastic acceleration, where particles gain energy in random steps. Spectral change fits stochastic acceleration well. On three nights the model develops a Maxwellian pile-up component as acceleration gives way to cooling, a pattern also hinted by high-energy and X-ray light curves.
arxiv-2604-20580: Faulconnier and four colleagues study laddering, the spread of a topological defect, in knitted fabrics after thread breaks or dropped stitches. They test a pre-stressed knit with experiments and Discrete Element Rod simulations, varying tension on the fabric. A force threshold from stitch curvature controls start and stop of propagation, as tension relaxes through freed thread length, enabling damage prediction. Ladder speed runs near bending-wave speed and scales linearly with tension, from elastic and friction forces. The findings speak to damage control in architected materials.
arxiv-2604-20880: Faizal and Shabir show how circle compactification makes abelian anomalies in F-theory concrete, encoding them in quantized Chern-Simons couplings of a three-dimensional theory. They compute those couplings twice, from M-theory flux terms and from a one-loop sum over the full massive spectrum, and the match fixes every normalization. Compatibility with type IIB modular duality follows once a known duality counterterm is added, illustrated by an explicit rank-two example.
arxiv-2604-21080: Tomás Ferreira Chase and Diana López Nacir compute the gravitational waves thrown off as an ultralight vector dark-matter field evolves. Because a uniform vector background breaks spatial symmetry, scalar ripples feed into tensor ripples, seeding a background of gravitational waves. Built into a modified cosmology code, their calculation yields the present-day spectrum such waves would leave behind.
arxiv-2604-21180: Aditya Sai Pranith Ayapilla and three colleagues build DiffSRDA, a method that blends thin, noisy observations into forecasts of chaotic fluid flows. It learns offline from coarse forecasts plus scattered sharp observations, then samples sets of sharp analyses that show honest uncertainty. It nearly matches a Kalman filter fed costly sharp forecasts, keeps most accuracy with only a few diffusion steps, and adapts to new sensor layouts without retraining.
arxiv-2604-21280: Jebacyril Arockiaraj, Dhruv Parikh, and Viktor Prasanna build ImageHD, a chip accelerator that lets edge devices keep learning from streaming images without backpropagation or bulky stored examples. Hyperdimensional computing updates fast and non-iteratively, and a compact convolutional front end supplies strong visual features. A hardware-aware method bounds stored exemplars and merges clusters efficiently on an AMD Zynq FPGA. On CORe50 it runs about 40 times faster and 383 times more energy-efficiently than tuned CPU baselines.
arxiv-2604-21480: Itay Nakash, George Kour, and Ateret Anaby-Tavor make agent testing cheaper and more thorough with DIVERT, a snapshot-based, coverage-guided user simulation system. Standard linear rollouts redo identical early prefixes and miss deep failures from rare user behaviors. DIVERT captures full agent-environment state at key decision points and resumes from snapshots, reusing shared prefixes. From each junction it branches with targeted, diversity-inducing user responses, exploring other paths. The method finds more failures per token than linear rollouts and widens the set of tasks where failures surface.
arxiv-2604-21680: Saha and Ramdas study e-variables, tools for safe inference that stays valid at any stopping time. The best unconstrained e-variable comes from the likelihood ratio of least favourable distributions, but real settings may add privacy, quantisation, boundedness, or moment limits. They show the constrained optimum often follows a simple optimise-then-constrain rule: compute the unconstrained optimum first, then transform it to meet the constraint, with no need for a new distribution pair.
arxiv-2604-21780: Höfling and five colleagues question what model-brain alignment benchmarks actually prove. Standard pipelines rank diverse vision models as roughly equivalent on the BOLD Moments video fMRI dataset, showing weak discriminative power. The authors instead test alignment patterns, each brain region's profile of relations to all other regions. Those patterns stay stable across different subjects' brains, yet even top-ranked models often fail to reproduce them. Alignment for prediction, they argue, differs from alignment as a model of human visual cortex.
arxiv-2604-21880: Chou, Wang, and Wu study the generalized Lamé equation on an elliptic curve with singularities. By analysing the locus admitting quasi-periodic solutions, they construct two curves. The first is the generalized Lamé curve, parametrising Hermite-Halphen solutions. The second is the log-free curve, arising when weights lie in half the natural numbers, which they prove is a reduced curve, confirming Wang's conjecture. The addition map gives a degree formula, and degenerations under pole collisions mirror the tensor algebra of sl2 modules in the BGG category O.
arxiv-2604-21980: Poppitz studies self-dual instantons of topological charge Q=r/N in SU(N) Yang-Mills theory on a four torus with 't Hooft twists, by embedding them into D-brane theories. He constructs wrapped brane configurations dual to constant field strength instanton backgrounds. Locally, the moduli space is identified with the Higgs branch of an N=2 supersymmetric theory. This parameterization matches one found in field theory, with hyper-Kähler structure. Combining perspectives on instantons on the torus will help understand the global structure of the moduli space.
arxiv-2604-22080: Fa and Culjak argue that LLM-based agents, fast-spreading in scientific data analysis, speed a known failure. They enable the rapid production of plausible endless rewrites, turning hypothesis space into claims backed by hand-picked work. Tests that could have disproven the claim never ran or never appeared. The authors propose a fail-first rule for lab-free claims made with agent help. Agents should hunt for failure modes of the claim, not craft the most compelling narrative.
arxiv-2604-22380: Iwaya and three colleagues speed gravitational-wave estimates for binary neutron star signals, which can last several minutes. Neural posterior estimation is fast but needs strong cuts to large input data. Their compression builds summary stats from relative binning, condensing frequency data via a polynomial fit of the waveform ratio. Training and storage costs then beat past networks for such inference. Checked against nested sampling over 1024 injections, their network gives well-calibrated posteriors, with gaps near numerical noise for most cases.
arxiv-2604-22580: Essafouri and three colleagues tackle accounts of network forecasts on dynamic physical fields, as in autoregressive weather forecasting. Explaining forecasts moved from curiosity to a strict need in high-stakes settings. Gradient-based feature attribution is widely used for high-dimensional inputs. On images, SmoothGrad firms up accounts by averaging attribution maps from noised inputs, and the authors aim to adapt it to dynamic fields. Their finding pinpoints a failure mode in averaging perturbed attribution maps on dynamic fields: stochastic perturbations do not induce steady amplitude noise in the maps.
arxiv-2604-22680: Sinha and Thapa review dense matter in compact stars under strong magnetic fields. Compact stars hold matter at densities far past lab reach. Magnetars may hold inside fields near 10^17-10^18 gauss. Such extremes shift small- and large-scale traits of dense matter. The review looks at how strong fields shape fermionic matter via Landau quantization and odd magnetic moment effects. It covers magnetized hadronic matter in relativistic mean-field models, plus hyperons, Delta resonances, meson condensates, and quark matter. Effects on neutron-star structure and sky limits are sketched.
arxiv-2604-23080: Dazzi and three colleagues study spread-out agent discovery under two-level churn in large agentic systems on spread setup. Node churn comes from failures and host exits; agent churn comes from demand-driven activation, sleep, and state changes. Using Kademlia as a baseline and Cyclon+Vicinity as a gossip baseline, they compare stable, node-only, agent-cooling-only, and joint regimes. Structured overlays prove more robust and fast in stable and node regimes, while gossip overlays stay close and can be faster when being ready matters most.
arxiv-2604-23380: Tang and colleagues make online reinforcement learning practical for image-making diffusion models, whose exact likelihoods cannot be computed directly. They rebuild the evidence-lower-bound surrogate approach with lower-variance estimates and controlled gradient steps, pairing it with group-relative policy optimization. The resulting method, V-GRPO, sets a new mark in text-to-image generation while running twice as fast as one rival method and three times as fast as another.
arxiv-2604-23580: Xie and colleagues introduce PhysCodeBench, the first benchmark that tests whether language models can turn physics descriptions into code that simulates the right physics, not merely code that runs. Its 1,200 expert-checked examples span four domains, and scoring checks conservation laws and expert assertions straight from the engine state. Their multi-agent correction method nearly triples the best proprietary baseline's pass rate.
arxiv-2604-23680: Zhou offers a single picture-based reading of hidden zeros and two-splits of tree-level scattering amplitudes. The trick is shuffle splitting along a set line. It splits Feynman diagrams after summing over shuffle orders. The reading unifies three cases. Hidden zeros trace to the on-shell rule of a massless particle. Two-splits come from splitting each diagram along two lines, like two zippers coming apart.
arxiv-2604-23780: Huang, Boscarino, and Xiong build a fully high-order asymptotic-preserving (AP) scheme for shallow-water flows. The flows include non-flat bottoms and Manning friction. Their earlier penalty version was stable but costly and slow to converge in the middle regime. Dropping the penalty keeps AP working. A mixed Runge-Kutta time step plus a high-order spatial rebuild gives speed gains. Solving friction inside the time step proves key to keep it stable.
arxiv-2604-23880: Wang and colleagues present a coordinated multipoint anti-jamming beam synthesis scheme that replaces costly optimisation with deep unfolding. Access points set analog beams from local angle data, while a central unit does cooperative digital beamforming with a single interaction, slashing fronthaul overhead. Turning step-size search into a trainable parameter cuts single-access-point runtime by about two-thirds. Hardware tests on an ARM-FPGA platform plus anechoic chamber measurements confirm robust real-world performance.
arxiv-2604-23980: Zhang and three colleagues tackle decentralized Muon, where the matrix-sign step refuses to commute with gossip averaging. Their SUDA template splits modular parts from non-modular ones, with ED/D-squared, EXTRA, and gradient tracking as backbones. They prove a topology-separated convergence guarantee whose main term skips graph quantities, plus two non-modular boundaries: tracking must precede polarization, and no server-free method can run the average-then-polarize update. Tests on CIFAR-100 and GPT-2 fine-tuning support it, with SUDA-Muon ahead in non-IID settings.
arxiv-2604-24080: Nishimoto and Tabei present the dynamic RR-index, the first dynamic self-index to reach delta-optimal space for repetitive strings. Static indexes already meet the bound, but dynamic versions missed it, paid logarithmic time per hit, or slowed with the longest common prefix maximum. Built on restricted recompression run-length programs, it stores delta-optimal bits in expectation, answers locate queries fast, and updates without longest-prefix dependence. On eleven corpora it runs up to 77 times faster on updates and up to 11 times faster on locate queries than rivals.
arxiv-2604-24480: Schadner shows Black-Scholes implied volatility is a quantile. The normalized option price acts as a probability on the variance scale, with the inverse Gaussian distribution linking price and volatility. This yields exact formulas for implied volatility from quantile functions, with only observable option inputs on the right. The result rewrites the price-volatility map as a distributional transform, gives implied volatility a first-passage interpretation, and identifies variance as the inversion coordinate. The formula reaches machine precision faster than a leading solver in the benchmark considered.
arxiv-2604-24580: McDowall, Georgopoulos and Wallden propose a new schedule for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm. It uses the spectral gap, the energy separation in an adiabatic Hamiltonian, to slow evolution where the gap is small. Their Spectral Gap Informed Ramp method beats the linear-ramp version on Grover search at fixed depth. It also reaches the same success chance at shorter depth. Gains extend to maximum independent set problems and persist under mild noise.
arxiv-2604-25080: Nian and five colleagues present CacheFlow, fast LLM serving via KV cache restoration. Existing methods choose either recomputation of cached states or loading them from storage. They overlook parallelism within models and contention across requests. CacheFlow rethinks restoration as parallel work across tokens, layers and GPUs.
